request: Add a rate-limiting decorator to CTFd that caps POST requests per client per time window, and apply it to the login, register and team forms.

summary.result_text:
I couldn't run the test: the sandbox blocked `pytest` and asked for approval, so none of this has been run.

`CTFd/auth.py` and `CTFd/teams.py` already imported and used a `ratelimit` decorator, but `CTFd/utils/decorators/__init__.py` only defined `throttle`. That meant the import failed. I fixed that and covered the one form that had no limit.

- **Decorator:** I renamed `throttle` to `ratelimit` in `CTFd/utils/decorators/__init__.py` and added a docstring. It counts requests of the given method per client IP and endpoint. Once the count passes `limit` within `interval` seconds, it returns a 429 JSON response. I changed the default cache key prefix from `th` to `rl`. Nothing else in the repo referenced `throttle`.
- **Where it applies:** `login` and `register` were already decorated at 10 POSTs per 5 seconds, as was `teams.join`. `teams.new`, the team creation form, had no limit, so I added `@ratelimit(method="POST", limit=10, interval=5)` to it in `CTFd/teams.py`.

To check it, run `python -m pytest tests/utils/test_ratelimit.py tests/teams/test_auth.py`.

input.pattern: ratelimit|def login|def register|def team|def new|def join

input.command: git status --short && git log --oneline | head -3 && grep -rn "throttle\|ratelimit" CTFd/auth.py CTFd/teams.py tests/utils/test_ratelimit.py CTFd/utils/decorators/ | head -30
grep -rn "throttle" --include=*.py . | grep -v "^./CTFd/utils/decorators/__init__" ; sed -n 120,130p CTFd/teams.py; sed -n 186,194p CTFd/teams.py; sed -n 1,30p tests/utils/test_ratelimit.py
